title: Module 9: Additional App Development Topics
description: The Service Catalog and record producers as a friendly application interface (catalog UI policies, catalog client scripts, and server-side producer scripting), plus ServiceNow developer resources.

questions.prompt: How is the Service Catalog best described?

choices.text: A categorical listing of things that can be ordered or requested
A scheduled background job that imports data from external source files
A tool for debugging server-side business rule scripts
A framework for running automated regression tests

questions.explanation: The Service Catalog is a categorical listing of items and services users can order or request, presented as a user-friendly, e-commerce-like replacement for forms. It is part of the Self-Service application.

questions.prompt: What license is required to use the Service Catalog?

choices.text: A separate Service Catalog subscription must be purchased
No license is required; it is part of the Self-Service application
An Integration Hub subscription is required before the catalog can be enabled
A per-user catalog license is required for each requester

questions.explanation: No license is required to use the Service Catalog. It is part of the ServiceNow Self-Service application.

questions.prompt: What is the outcome of submitting a record producer (as opposed to a standard catalog item)?

choices.text: A request with requested items and catalog tasks is generated
A record is inserted into a table chosen by the developer
An approval workflow is started for the requested service
An email notification is queued for the fulfillment group

questions.explanation: A record producer inserts a record directly into a table chosen by the developer, with no request (REQ), requested items (RITM), or catalog tasks. The REQ/RITM/task outcome belongs to standard catalog items.

questions.prompt: When a standard catalog item is ordered, how do the resulting records relate?

choices.text: Each task is the parent of its request, which contains the items
Each requested item is a child of a request and references a catalog item
The request and the requested item are stored in the same single record
The catalog item is a child of the task generated to fulfill it

questions.explanation: Ordering a catalog item creates a request (REQ) containing one or more requested items (RITM). Each RITM is a child of the REQ and references the catalog item it was ordered from; RITMs may then spawn catalog tasks.

questions.prompt: How does closure roll up for a standard catalog request?

choices.text: Closing the request automatically closes all of its requested items and tasks
Each requested item must be closed manually after its request is closed
When a requested item's tasks all close it closes, and when all items close the request auto-closes
Tasks remain open until an administrator closes the parent request

questions.explanation: Closure rolls up from the bottom: when all of a requested item's tasks close, the RITM closes; once all RITMs are closed, the request (REQ) auto-closes.

questions.prompt: What is a record producer?

choices.text: A special type of Service Catalog item that creates a record in a database table
A background script that periodically generates summary records
A business rule that runs after a catalog request is approved
A reporting widget that produces charts and dashboards from catalog request data over time

questions.explanation: A record producer is a special type of Service Catalog item that is an alternative to the traditional form; both create a new record in a database table. Users answer questions that populate fields on the new record.

questions.prompt: Which requirement points toward using a classic form rather than a Service Catalog record producer?

choices.text: Users place an order by answering a few simple questions
Users need access to lists and the ability to edit existing records
The interface should include rich HTML, hyperlinks, images, and other graphics
The users of the interface are not highly technical

questions.explanation: Classic forms are the better choice when users need access to lists and context menus, the ability to personalize the UI, and the ability to edit existing records. The catalog suits ordering via simple questions for non-technical users.

questions.prompt: On a record producer, what are the input controls (the things that look like form fields) actually called?

choices.text: Columns
Dictionary entries
Variables
Attributes

questions.explanation: On a catalog item or record producer, the inputs are variables (stored in a catalog variable table with their own special types), not table columns. They map to fields on the produced record.

questions.prompt: Which related link on a table record is used to create a record producer?

choices.text: Show Schema Map
Add to Service Catalog
Explore REST API
Force to Update Set

questions.explanation: The Add to Service Catalog related link on a table record creates a record producer; the records it produces are created in that open table.

questions.prompt: In a server-side record producer script, what does the producer object represent?

choices.text: The new record that is currently being inserted into the chosen target table
The variables (answers) entered on the record producer form
The previous version of the record before it was changed
The catalog category the item was submitted from

questions.explanation: In a record producer script, producer represents the variables on the producer form (accessed as producer.<variableName>), while current represents the new record being produced on the target table.

questions.prompt: Why should you NOT call current.update() in a record producer script?

choices.text: Because the record is inserted automatically when the script finishes
Because current is read-only inside a record producer script
Because update() is not part of the scoped application API
Because doing so would redirect the user away from the catalog interface entirely

questions.explanation: The record producer inserts the current record automatically once the script completes, so calling current.update() (or current.insert()) is unnecessary and should be avoided.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the producer.redirect property?

choices.text: It validates all of the variable values on the form before the record is saved
It sets where the user is sent after submitting the record producer
It copies producer variables onto the current record
It restricts which roles can open the record producer

questions.explanation: producer.redirect takes a relative path that determines where the user goes after submitting. Because catalogs have no lists, a redirect script is auto-created so the user lands on a chosen page rather than a list view.

questions.prompt: Which pair of variable types defines the sections used to build a multi-column record producer layout?

choices.text: Section Open and Section Close
Layout Begin and Layout Finish
Container Start and Container End
Row Header and Row Footer

questions.explanation: Columns are defined with Container Start and Container End variable types; the Container Start specifies the column layout for that section, and the Order column positions them.

questions.prompt: What can a Catalog UI Policy do without any scripting?

choices.text: Make a variable visible, read-only, or mandatory
Send an outbound REST request to an external web service provider
Insert a related record into another table
Generate an event in the event queue

questions.explanation: Catalog UI Policy Actions can make a variable visible, read-only, or mandatory with no scripting. A client-side script can optionally be added by enabling Run Scripts and using the Execute if true/false fields.

questions.prompt: To what can a Catalog Client Script be applied?

choices.text: Only to a single database table at a time
An individual catalog item or a variable set
Only to the global Service Catalog as a whole
Any server-side business rule on the target table

questions.explanation: Catalog Client Scripts can be applied to an individual catalog item or to a variable set, and the variables available to them come from the questions on the form.

questions.prompt: On which side(s) do Service Catalog item scripts execute?

choices.text: On the client side only
On the server side only
On both the client and server sides
Only inside the MID Server process

questions.explanation: Service Catalog item scripts execute on both the client side (catalog client scripts, catalog UI policies) and the server side (record producer scripts).

questions.prompt: When configuring a record producer, what does the Short description field control?

choices.text: The text shown in a pop-up when the user hovers over the item
The name that is displayed for the item throughout the Service Catalog
The category the item is placed into
The list of variables that appear on the form

questions.explanation: Short description is the text shown in a pop-up when a user hovers over the item. Name is the item's displayed text, Category is where it appears, and the selected variables are the form fields.

questions.prompt: Which link type and argument are used to make a navigator module open a record producer?

choices.text: Link type Map Page, configured with the record producer's name set as the target page
Link type URL (from Arguments), with sysparm_id set to the record producer sys_id
Link type List of Records, filtered to the catalog item table
Link type Separator, with the category name as the argument

questions.explanation: The module uses Link type URL (from Arguments) with com.glideapp.servicecatalog_cat_item_view.do?v=1&sysparm_id=<record producer sys_id>. The sys_id is obtained by right-clicking the record producer header and choosing Copy sys_id.

questions.prompt: Which category field is used to build a hierarchy of sub-categories?

choices.text: Location
Homepage renderer
Parent
Header icon

questions.explanation: The Parent field designates a category's parent, allowing a hierarchy of sub-categories. Roles control who may order, and the various icon fields control graphics.

questions.prompt: Why might a newly created category not appear in the Service Catalog?

choices.text: Categories only become visible after a full instance cache flush is performed
A category with no items or record producers assigned does not appear
Categories require a separate license before they are visible
Categories are hidden until an approval workflow completes

questions.explanation: A category that has no record producers or catalog items assigned to it will not appear in the catalog list.

questions.prompt: Which statement about applications on the ServiceNow Developer Share site is correct?

choices.text: They are certified by ServiceNow and available for a fee
They are not vetted by ServiceNow and are available at no cost
They are reviewed by ServiceNow and installable on any instance
They require joining the Partner Program before download

questions.explanation: Developer Share applications are not vetted by ServiceNow and are all available at no cost. Certification and review apply to ServiceNow Store apps, not Developer Share.

questions.prompt: Which statement about applications on the ServiceNow Store is correct?

choices.text: They are all free, because the Store does not support paid apps
They are uploaded without review by any ServiceNow process
They are certified by ServiceNow, and some are free while others are fee-based
They can only ever be installed on the same instance that originally created them

questions.explanation: ServiceNow Store apps are certified for compliance with best practices and, after review and approval, can be installed on any instance running a supported version. Some are free and some are fee-based; developers distribute them via the Partner Program.

questions.prompt: Where do you obtain a Personal Developer Instance (PDI) and the JavaScript API documentation?

choices.text: The Developer portal at developer.servicenow.com
The ServiceNow Store at store.servicenow.com
The product documentation at docs.servicenow.com
The instance's own System Definition module

questions.explanation: The Developer portal (developer.servicenow.com) provides the JavaScript API documentation, the Developer Share site, and Personal Developer Instances. docs.servicenow.com hosts product documentation and release notes.
